Please turn each photo I upload into an independent high-end design poster, no multi-image stitching, each photo output individually. Overall use a 3:4 vertical composition, the top and bottom areas are strictly 1:1 in height, each occupying 50% of the screen.

The upper half retains the original photo, maintaining the subject's identity, structure, posture, real texture, natural light and shadow, and original color atmosphere, with only slight high-end color grading to give it the texture of art magazines and exhibition images. To adapt to the frame size, the environmental background can be naturally extended, but the subject must not be stretched, distorted, or changed.

The lower half performs new artistic judgment, only extracting the most recognizable subject, outline, structure, posture, and narrative relationship from the photo, reconstructed as Hand-drawn Doodle Lifestyle Illustration / Naïve Illustration / Marker Drawing. Do not retain all objects, do not copy the original scene; actively delete the vast majority of backgrounds and irrelevant information, re-direct the scene through deletion, reorganization, cropping, and scale changes, so that even if the original image has an ordinary composition, it can be transformed into a valid piece of work.

Modeling is simplified, symbolic, relaxed, and personalized, using slightly jittery, intermittent, and not completely regular hand-drawn lines, as well as natural coloring like markers, crayons, and oil pastels. Allow slight line crossing, white space, and manual errors, without pursuing realistic proportions, complete perspective, or fine depiction.

The lower half must take a huge amount of conscious whitespace as its core, with solid graphics occupying only a small proportion, and the rest of the space actively left blank. Subjects can be eccentric, edge-aligned, suspended, or partially cropped, with positions determined by posture direction and visual center of gravity. Whitespace and the subject together form positive and negative shapes, distance, pauses, and a sense of breathing; rather paint less than fill the screen.

Graphics and text must be re-typeset as a whole, rather than “a sentence on top, a character below.” Establish an invisible grid, visual axis, and reading path first, then decide on text placement; text can be close to the subject's outline, follow the direction of movement, align with the head or shoulder line, fall in large negative spaces, or form staggered, interspersed, and asymmetrical echoes with the graphics. Avoid mechanical centering, top-to-bottom stacking, and fixed templates; let graphics handle emotion and text handle rhythm, with both completing the composition together.

Text has no language restriction, retaining only a very small amount of truly meaningful words or short phrases. Use light, natural handwritten fonts with slight variations in character width and pen pressure, keeping a bit of a casual writing feel, but letter spacing, line spacing, and overall placement must be controlled through editorial design. One slightly obvious short phrase can be used with tiny auxiliary text to form a hierarchy, but no menu-style titles, long copy, or full-page text.

Color adopts a soft, bright, and healing limited palette, re-modulating the most vital colors extracted from the original image to form refreshing colors such as cream yellow, peach pink, coral red, sky blue, lake cyan, tender green, and lavender purple; vivid but not glaring, soft but not dirty-grey, with warm white or extremely light composite colors as large areas of breathing space.

Overall pursuit of naive drawing, mature composition, smart text-graphic relationships, and a massive amount of whitespace, like high-end independent magazines, lifestyle editorial illustrations, or art publications, rather than children's scrapbooks. Avoid fixed structures of centered subject + centered copy, random small icons scattered around, complex backgrounds, information accumulation, filling the screen, cheap cartoonishness, and templated layout.

Current user-approved edit specification, overriding conflicting layout above:
Horizontal 16:9, equal left original and right doodle. Small woman with pink ribbon, white sweater, floral skirt and loose bicycle outline, 20% occupied right-panel area, three controlled gesture lines, cream whitespace. Text SLOW AFTERNOON.
Preserve original image panel faithfully, no stretching. Input is AI-generated, not a real-world photograph. No extra people, no male characters or male hands.

posts.translation_zh:
请将我上传的每一张照片都转化为一张独立的高端设计海报，不要多图拼接，每张照片单独输出。整体采用 3:4 竖版构图，上下区域高度严格为 1:1，各占画面的 50%。

上半部分保留原始照片，保持主体的身份、结构、姿态、真实质感、自然光影和原有色彩氛围，只进行轻微的高级感调色，使其具有艺术杂志和展览图像的质感。为适配画面尺寸，可以自然延展环境背景，但主体不得被拉伸、扭曲或改变。

下半部分进行新的艺术判断，只从照片中提取最具辨识度的主体、轮廓、结构、姿态和叙事关系，重构为 Hand-drawn Doodle Lifestyle Illustration / Naïve Illustration / Marker Drawing。不要保留所有物体，不要复制原场景；要通过删除、重组、裁切和比例变化，主动删除绝大多数背景和无关信息，重新引导场景，使即使原图构图普通，也能转化为一件有效的作品。

造型应简化、符号化、放松且个性化，使用略微抖动、断续、不完全规则的手绘线条，以及像马克笔、蜡笔和油画棒一样的自然上色。允许轻微的线条交叉、留白和手工误差，不追求写实比例、完整透视或精细描绘。

下半部分必须以大量有意识的留白为核心，实体图形只占很小比例，其余空间主动留空。主体可以偏心、贴边、悬浮或部分裁切，位置由姿态方向和视觉重心决定。留白与主体共同形成正负形、距离、停顿和呼吸感；宁可少画，也不要填满画面。

图形与文字必须作为一个整体重新排版，而不是“上面一句话，下面一个人物”。先建立隐形网格、视觉轴线和阅读路径，再决定文字位置；文字可以贴近主体轮廓、顺应运动方向、与头部或肩线对齐、落在大面积负空间中，或与图形形成错落、穿插、不对称的呼应。避免机械居中、从上到下堆叠和固定模板；让图形负责情绪，文字负责节奏，两者共同完成构图。

文字不限语言，只保留极少量真正有意义的词语或短语。使用轻盈、自然的手写字体，字符宽度和笔压有轻微变化，保留一点随手书写感，但字距、行距和整体位置必须通过编辑设计加以控制。可以使用一个略明显的短句搭配极小的辅助文字来形成层级，但不要菜单式标题、长文案或满版文字。

色彩采用柔和、明亮且治愈的限定调色板，将从原图中提取出的最具生命力的颜色重新调和，形成奶油黄、蜜桃粉、珊瑚红、天空蓝、湖水青、嫩绿和薰衣草紫等清爽色彩；鲜明但不刺眼，柔和但不脏灰，并以暖白色或极浅的复合色作为大面积的呼吸空间。

整体追求天真的绘画感、成熟的构图、灵巧的图文关系和大量留白，像高端独立杂志、生活方式编辑插画或艺术出版物，而不是儿童剪贴簿。避免固定的“居中主体 + 居中文案”结构、随机散落的小图标、复杂背景、信息堆积、填满屏幕、廉价的卡通感和模板化版式。

当前用户批准的编辑规格，优先于上方有冲突的布局：
横向 16:9，左侧原图与右侧涂鸦等宽。小女人，粉色丝带、白色毛衣、花卉半身裙和松散的自行车轮廓，占右侧面板面积的 20%，三条受控的手势线，奶油色留白。文字 SLOW AFTERNOON。
忠实保留原始图像面板，不要拉伸。输入为 AI 生成，不是真实世界照片。不要额外人物，不要男性角色或男性手部。
